market.summary: Indian indices ended flat after a choppy day (Nifty +0.18% to 25,299), but the broader market was firmer: midcaps +0.9%, smallcaps +1.1% and more stocks rose than fell. Foreign investors keep buying heavily and crude is easing, which supports risk appetite; media stocks were among the best sectors, which helps Tips Music. The rupee weakened to about 94 per dollar, a cost for importers but not a direct issue for these holdings.

points.text: Sensex closed +32 points at 81,911 and Nifty +44 points at 25,299; Nifty Midcap +0.9%, Smallcap +1.1%; 2,377 NSE stocks rose and 1,878 fell.
Realty (+3.7%) and Media (+2.4%) led; Auto (-1.0%), FMCG (-0.9%) and Pharma (-0.6%) lagged.
Foreign investors bought Rs 12,563 Cr of shares on 11 Nov; November net foreign buying is about $6.4 bn, the most since Sept 2024.
On 11 Nov the Nasdaq rose 1.6% and the S&P 500 1.3%; Brent fell about 1% to near $91.8.
Rupee ended at 94.03 per dollar, 34 paise weaker.

market.watch: Whether foreign buying continues and smallcaps keep outperforming; a sharp rupee fall or crude back above $95 would be a headwind.

GROWW.summary: No new company filing since the last read. The news that matters is the 6 Nov block trade of about 8.85 crore shares (1.4% of the company), which knocked the stock about 7% after a nine-day run; buyer and seller were not disclosed. The stock has since recovered to Rs 221.66, close to +2R, so the supply looks absorbed and accumulation continues; Jefferies kept Buy but trimmed its target to Rs 240.

points.text: 6 Nov: block deals of about 8.85 crore shares (~1.41% of equity); stock fell ~7%, ending a 9-day, 23% rally.
Q2 FY27: profit Rs 725 Cr (+54%), revenue Rs 1,541 Cr (+44%), transacting users 2.4 crore (+27%).
Jefferies: Buy retained, target cut to Rs 240 from Rs 250.

GROWW.watch: A close at Rs 224.90 is +2R (book half); the swing stop is Rs 205.33 (21 EMA).
